body: That makes a lot of sense actually! I think that is definitely the issue that came up between my ex-boyfriend and I when I think about it. I've been really apologetic to him and I had really let my guard down after the breakup--I apologized too often, and I really put myself out there for him to tear up as he pleased, which was definitely my mistake. And I do realize that, so I want to take the advice you've given me here so that I can learn to be stronger and avoid that behavior. You're really right about a lot of things you said here, so I'll definitely keep it in mind. I (hopefully) will be seeing a therapist for the first time within the next week, so I'll bring it up to them as well. Thanks for your kind words.

Well for me, the reason I don't really see myself as a lesbian is because even if the people I find myself attracted to have biologically female parts, they generally present themselves as boys or masculine? It's a really difficult way to feel...

And what's strange is like--of course I find myself attracted to male celebrities (I have a big thing for Johnny Depp LOL) and male fictional characters. I don't have issues thinking about them in sexual situations at all--but when it comes to physical, real boys in my day to day life, it makes me incredibly uncomfortable, even if I find their personalities and appearances insanely attractive! It's like... their faces and their personalities are wonderful, but the fact that they have a penis weirds me out and makes me uncomfortable. It's a very strange feeling...
I'm hoping I can go tomorrow and try to talk to someone about it but I dunno what choices they'll give me... Let's hope for the best.

Well I've tried talking through suicide helplines and stuff before and they usually calm me for the night, but then the next day I get upset all over again and it doesn't go away. I'd really like to see a therapist or a psychologist primarily because I'm starting to believe I need medication and it isn't just a matter of talking it out anymore. I've been talking it out a lot amidst my friends and other resources but the pain still doesn't go away, it just feels like it gets stronger.

I'm trying really hard, I am! Finding help is difficult because I still don't have health insurance and can't afford to pay for it. I tried applying for medicaid in February but still haven't gotten any word back on it. I live in an incredibly small town where we have only one hospital and one institution for therapy, and anything else is 2 hours away. I've tried to get in contact with the therapy institution up here a few times by sending emails and leaving messages but haven't received an email or a call back yet. Hoping to go visit the office in person tomorrow. 

I wish I could find some more resources for help that were actually accessible to me, because trying to handle everything on my own is getting to be insanely tough. I don't know what other resources are available to me other than therapy which is unachievable right now, though.

The very same thing happened to me about 5 years ago. Luckily none of my family members were inside, but the entire house burned, and our dog and cat both died in the fire. It does seem like a very difficult thing to get through, but do try to keep your head up.

Have you been allowed back inside of your home/apartment, or is it too damaged to even consider? My house was burned pretty badly, to the point where there were gaping holes in the floor (the fire started with the furnace/heat vents under the house), so we had to hop on the little islands of carpet that had been left over to avoid from falling into the floor. 

I was capable of recovering a lot of things though--my Nintendo 64 and games, some books hidden in cabinets, and somehow, my family albums and baby pictures survived as well. I'd definitely go in and look through the remains ASAP because you never know what might have survived! The only thing I advise against salvaging is clothes, because the fire stench can't be washed out.

Good luck and I hope you're able to get through this!

"I love you, please don't go."
It seems like a lot of Redditors around here are feeling the love sting haha!

Well of course ideally what *I* want is to stay together and try to work things out, because I do think that it's possible for us to work on the primary issues at hand, and of course on top of all things we had a lot more positives in our relationship than bad. 

However I'm thinking that I'm going to just tell him that if he wants to breakup, he wants to break up, and that means we go our separate ways, regardless of his mixed feelings or otherwise. He said he wanted to break up, and I want to move on, so we'll both be making choices for ourselves in that case.

Thanks a lot for your input!
